title: Length of the Final Word
statement:
You get a string s made of English letters and spaces. A word is a maximal run of letters with no spaces in it. Return the length of the last word in s.

The string may start or end with spaces, and words may be separated by more than one space. It always contains at least one word.

examples.why: The trailing spaces are not a word. The last word is "bags".
One word with no spaces at all.
Leading spaces and long gaps do not matter; only the run of letters at the end counts.

constraints: s contains only English letters and spaces
s contains at least one letter
hints: Do you need to look at the beginning of the string at all?
Start from the last character. What do you skip first, and when do you start counting?
Move left past trailing spaces, then count letters until you hit a space or the start of the string.

explain.intuition:
The answer lives at the end of the string, so read it from the end. First skip any trailing spaces; the first letter you then meet is the last letter of the last word. Keep walking left and counting until you hit a space or run out of string.

Splitting on spaces also works, but it builds every word just to look at one, and a naive split(" ") leaves empty strings for the trailing spaces, which is the classic way to return 0 by accident.
steps: While s[i] is a space, move i left.
While i ≥ 0 and s[i] is not a space, count it and move left.
pitfalls: Using s.split(" ") and taking the last element. With trailing spaces that element is an empty string.
Counting the trailing spaces as part of the word, or stopping at the first space you meet from the end.
Running off the front of the string when the whole input is one word.

complexity.time: O(n) worst case, only the tail is read

solutions.title: Split into words
solutions.idea: Trim, split on runs of spaces, and measure the last piece.

solutions.title: Scan backwards from the end
solutions.idea: Skip trailing spaces, then count letters until the next space or the start.

followups: Return the length of the longest word instead. Can you still do it in one pass with O(1) space?
The text is a stream you can only read once from the start. How do you track the last word?
